intro: A Skilled Worker visa extension lets you stay in your job with the same sponsor. Salary rules have changed, so we check which thresholds apply to you before your Skilled Worker visa extension goes in.

rules.title: Which rules apply to you?
rules.text: People first sponsored before 22 July 2025 may keep older, lower skill and salary thresholds in some situations. We check your history.

rules.title: Apply in time
rules.text: Apply before your current visa expires to keep your continuous residence.

rules.title: Settlement
rules.text: Under the government’s plans, Skilled Workers earning £50,271 or more in 3 of the last 5 years keep a 5-year route to ILR. [Read about the ILR changes](/ilr-changes-2026/)

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: Skilled Worker visa extension requirements
sections.text: You need a new Certificate of Sponsorship from your current employer, a job that still meets the skill level and salary rules that apply to you, and to apply before your current visa expires. You usually don’t need to prove your English again.

faqs.q: Do I need a new CoS for a Skilled Worker visa extension?
faqs.a: Yes. Your employer assigns a new Certificate of Sponsorship.

faqs.q: Can my family extend with me?
faqs.a: Yes, your dependants can apply at the same time.

faqs.q: Do I need another English test?
faqs.a: Usually not, if you proved it in an earlier Skilled Worker application.
